name: Why Traceability Matters
title: Why Traceability Matters
description: When a part fails, traceability answers: which other products contain it? When a design changes, it answers: which units have the old vs new? Without it, recalls are guesses and changes are chaos.
how_it_works: Implement traceability proportionate to risk: lot traceability for most, serial for critical. The cost of traceability is always less than the cost of its absence in a crisis.
key_points: Answers: where else is this part? which configuration?
requirements: Unique identification of parts and assemblies; recorded parent-child relationships; change records.
standards: Configuration management practice (EIA-649, ISO 10007); lot/serial traceability practice.
citations: EIA-649 configuration management standard.
ISO 10007 quality management - configuration management guidance.

name: Lot vs Serial Traceability
title: Lot vs Serial Traceability
description: Lot traceability tracks groups (this batch of resistors went into these products); serial tracks individuals (this exact unit). Serial costs more and tells more.
how_it_works: Choose lot for commodity parts, serial for critical/safety/regulated items, and record the linkage at each assembly step. The choice balances cost against recall precision.
requirements: Unique identification of parts and assemblies; recorded parent-child relationships; change records.
standards: Configuration management practice (EIA-649, ISO 10007); lot/serial traceability practice.
citations: EIA-649 configuration management standard.
